reqs.text: While viewing filter state that arrived from a URL, a "Back to my view" action is available. It discards the shared view and restores the user's own saved filters. It also clears any active search query, because the query is not part of saved state and there is nothing to restore it to. The label is deliberately "my view" rather than "my filters", since the action affects both filters and search

nonreq.text: Users managing large volumes of work orders need to quickly narrow down the list to a relevant subset: by status, customer, technician, advisor, or on-site asset status. Currently, the Work Orders page lacks a dedicated filter bar, forcing users to scroll through long lists or rely on the tab shortcuts (Estimates, Completed) as the only filtering mechanism. This makes day-to-day triage slower and increases the chance of missing urgent work orders. Adding a persistent, multi-criteria filter bar directly addresses this pain point and aligns ShopView with the workflow expectations of shop managers and service advisors.
A filter bar appears below the tab navigation on the Work Orders page, providing quick access to five filters: Status, Customer, Lead Technician, Service Advisor, and Asset on Site
Each filter is a labelled chip that opens a dropdown panel when clicked
Status, Customer, Lead Technician, and Service Advisor are multi-select filters; Asset on Site is a two-option (Yes / No) dropdown
Customer, Lead Technician, and Service Advisor dropdowns include a search field to quickly locate a specific value
When one or more values are selected in a filter, the chip updates to display the selected values and a "Clear filters" button appears in the filter bar
The filter bar can be collapsed and expanded via a toggle in the page toolbar; when collapsed with active filters, the toolbar toggle shows a visual indicator
Filter selections persist when the user navigates away from the Work Orders page and returns
The active filter state is reflected in the page URL, enabling users to share or bookmark a filtered view
Filters apply to all tabs except where noted (see Tab Behavior, Story 9)
Supported on both desktop and mobile

A filter bar appears below the page header on each view of the Parts area (Inventory, Part Sales, Catalog, Returns, Credits, Purchase Orders, Vendor Invoices, Vendors), following the same chip-and-dropdown pattern as Work Orders

Filters are context-specific per view: each view shows only the chips relevant to its data (e.g., Inventory filters by Bin Location, Category, Supply, and Vendor; Purchase Orders by Vendor, Status, Date, and Ordered by)

Entity filters (Customer, Vendor, Created by, Ordered by, Received by, Processed by) use the searchable multi-select dropdown; long lists such as Category and Manufacturer also include a search field; short attribute filters (Supply, Part Type, Bin Location, State/Province, Status) use the checkbox list
Date-based columns (Date, Invoice date, Date received) use the new date-range filter
Active-chip appearance, "Clear filters", "Clear selection", collapse/expand, per-view persistence, URL state, and mobile behavior all match the Work Orders definitions
A filter bar appears below the report header on each report, following the same chip-and-dropdown pattern as Work Orders

Filters are context-specific per report: nearly every report includes a Date filter as its primary scoping control, alongside the entity dimensions relevant to that report (Customer, Vendor, Technician, Advisor, Staff, Employee, and so on)

A new date-range filter type is introduced: the chip opens a start/end date picker with no presets and no default range selected, so the user always chooses the period, and the range applies immediately when the second date is picked. The selected range is reflected in the URL (e.g., range=custom&from=2026-04-01&to=2026-04-25) so a filtered report is shareable
Reports with sub-report tabs keep a separate filter set per tab
Active-chip appearance, "Clear filters", "Clear selection", collapse/expand, persistence, URL state, and mobile behavior all match the Work Orders definitions
Each list page gains a search control in the page toolbar, sitting alongside the filter bar toggle and the primary action. It narrows the records in that page's table only
The control is collapsed by default (magnifier icon + "Search") and expands in place into a text input when clicked, on both desktop and mobile
Search applies as the user types, with no apply button, and works additively with the filter bar: a query narrows within the active filters, and vice versa

Available on every table in the application, delivered through the shared table component: the list pages across Work Orders, Parts and Reports, plus tables on detail pages and in dialogs. Desktop and mobile
The query is scoped to the browser tab session rather than saved to the user account, unlike filters. See Key Decisions
Because page-level narrowing now lives on the page, the global header search stops filtering page content; this behaviour is removed app-wide (Story 14)

When I'm opening my work queue at the start of the day, I want to filter work orders by technician and status, so I can see exactly what's in progress for my team without scrolling through everything.
When a customer calls about their vehicle, I want to filter by customer name, so I can instantly see all their open work orders.
When I'm doing a lot check, I want to filter by "Asset on Site: Yes", so I can see only vehicles currently on premises.
When I'm counting stock, I want to filter Inventory by Bin Location and Category, so I can verify quantities for one shelf without scrolling the whole catalog.
When a vendor invoice arrives, I want to filter Vendor Invoices by Vendor and Date received, so I can find and reconcile the matching record quickly.
When I run month-end A/R aging, I want to set the Date range and filter by Customer, so I can produce the exact statement a customer is disputing.
When I review payroll, I want to filter Timesheets by Employee and a pay-period Date range, so I can approve hours for one person at a time.
When I know the work order number but not who it belongs to, I want to type it straight into the page, so I can jump to it without setting up a filter.
When I have already filtered Inventory down to one bin, I want to search within that result, so I can find one part without clearing my filters.
Reduce time to find a relevant subset of work orders
Allow multi-criteria filtering in a single interaction
Persist filter state to avoid re-applying filters on every visit
Enable sharing of filtered views via URL
Asset on Site changed from toggle to dropdown to maintain visual and interaction consistency with the other four filters, all of which use the dropdown chip pattern.
No selection limit on multi-select filters: users can select as many values as needed.
"Clear filters" clears all active filters at once; a separate "Clear selection" action within each dropdown clears only that filter individually.

Status filter is hidden on the Estimates and Completed tabs, because those tabs are shortcuts that already pre-filter by a single status, so showing a Status filter would be redundant and potentially confusing.

Imported is exclusive, not a status. Imported work orders come from a different data source, so selecting Imported switches the list to the imported records rather than filtering the existing set, and the other filter chips are disabled while it is active. Current production behaviour, unchanged by this work.
My Work Orders tab does not remove filters: filters continue to work on top of the user-scoped result set.

Filters persist across sessions, devices and logout: filter state is stored server-side against the user account, syncs across the user's devices, and survives logout. Where two devices write different state, last write wins. This applies uniformly, with no per-page exceptions.

A shared link never overwrites saved state: filter state carried in a URL applies at runtime only. Edits the user makes while viewing a shared link are not written back to their saved filters either. A "Back to my view" action returns them to their own state. The label covers filters and search together, since the action restores saved filters and clears any active query.

Context-specific filter sets on Parts and Reports: each Parts view and each Report defines its own filter chips rather than sharing a single set, because the underlying datasets and relevant dimensions differ per view.

New date-range filter type: Date chips open a custom start/end picker with no presets and no default range, and apply immediately on selection of the second date. Used across Reports and the date columns on Parts views.

Parts and Reports selections are scoped to their view/tab and persist there: filters do not carry across Parts views, Report tabs, or sub-report tabs; each view/tab retains its own selections and restores them on return. Scope and persistence are separate concerns: every one of those separate sets persists on the terms above.
Long enumerations get a search field: Category and Manufacturer use the searchable dropdown rather than a plain checkbox list.
Multi-select where it makes sense: all Parts and Reports filters are multi-select except the date-range filter, which is a single range.

Page search is separate from the filter bar, not a filter chip. It lives in the toolbar row with the collapse toggle and primary action; the chips stay in the row below. The two are additive but independently cleared: "Clear filters" does not clear the query, and clearing the query does not clear the chips.

Global search no longer filters page content. Narrowing the current list is now the job of the page's own filters and search. The global search filtering behaviour is removed across the whole application, not only on the pages covered by these designs.

One shared search component, scoped strictly to its own table. Page-specific behaviour is configuration (which fields are searched), not a per-module variant. Each search input queries only the records in its own table; it cannot reach content in any other table, on any other page, or in any other module. Cross-page and cross-module lookup is the job of the global header search, which is the whole basis for the split in Story 14.

The search query is deliberately not persisted the way filters are. It is scoped to the browser tab session rather than stored against the user account: it survives navigating away and returning, does not sync across devices, and each browser tab keeps its own. A search is momentary in a way a filter set is not, so returning to a list days later narrowed by something typed once would be surprising. The contrast with filter persistence above is intentional.

Generic placeholder. The expanded field reads "Type to search" on every page rather than being parameterised per page, unlike the filter dropdowns which use targeted copy ("Search customer", "Search technician").

Mobile and desktop use one pattern, not two. Search expands inline in the action row on both, with the same four component states. Two layout changes make this possible on a 370px mobile row: the primary CTA stops stretching and uses its natural hug width (144px for "New Work Order", the same as desktop) instead of filling the row at 211px; and pages with more than one icon-only action collapse those into a "more" kebab. Together these free enough space for the field to expand with every other control still visible. No modal, no separate search screen, no active-query indicator, and no mobile-only variant to maintain.
Hover-on-expanded, disabled and loading states are out of scope for this release; the component does not define them.

Mobile uses deferred apply: desktop filters in real time, while mobile stages the user's selections and applies them only when the user taps an "Apply filters" button — a deliberate difference for small-screen ergonomics (see Story 12).
As a user, I want to see a filter bar on the Work Orders page so that I can quickly narrow down the list.
